properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-24 on the v0.70.0 cut: a claim released before the cut makes step 6's export REFUSE as divergence, because the committed file still holds the CLAIMS edge the graph no longer has
properties.source: the v0.70.0 cut, run from the dev_reflow2 hub session
properties.statement:
The /jot claim was made on feat/jot and travelled into main's export with #586. It was released (release_claim) at the start of the cut, as AGENTS.md's order of operations says. Step 6's export onto the cut branch was then REFUSED by the stale-seat guard: "would DELETE 0 node(s) and 1 edge(s) … CLAIMS who:claude-code -> req:a-jot-…". That edge was not somebody else's work; it was the released claim, removed on purpose. The export went through with accept_divergence: true, and the commit message says why.

The lesson for the next cut: when the ONLY dropped item is a CLAIMS edge you released yourself, accept_divergence is correct; read the "Dropped:" line before passing it, because the same flag would discard real work. The guard cannot tell a released claim from a colleague's missing edit, and neither flow:release-cut nor release_claim says this will happen.
